rationale: The pain is real but narrowly scoped: operators self-host precisely to avoid paying for managed services, making willingness to pay for a monitoring/remediation tool structurally weak. Free alternatives (MXToolbox, mail-tester.com, UCEPROTECT's own lookup) already cover the diagnostic layer, and actual remediation of shared-range blocklist listings (especially UCEPROTECT L3, which requires ISP-level action or a $299 'express' fee paid to UCEPROTECT directly) is outside any third-party tool's control. The evidence base across public forums is thin — the source thread has low engagement and the signal strength was scored at 2 — falling short of the 5 distinct pain quotes required for a pass verdict.
